comments.body:
## RCA — confirmed root cause (Phase 1 complete)

**The detector is NOT broken. The test fixture has never been detectable.**

### Mechanism

`test_live_clone` writes two byte-identical 7-line JS files. That duplicated fragment is
**32 tokens**. jscpd's default `--min-tokens` is **50**, so no clone fragment in the fixture
can ever reach the detection floor, and jscpd correctly reports `clones: 0`.

Evidence (jscpd 5.0.14, `jscpd --debug` config dump on the exact fixture):

    "min_tokens": 50,
    "min_lines": 5,

Same fixture, floor lowered:

    jscpd --min-tokens 50 ./src -> {'clones': 0, 'sources': 0, 'tokens': 0}
    jscpd --min-tokens 10 ./src -> {'clones': 1, 'sources': 2, 'tokens': 64,
                                    'duplicatedTokens': 32, 'percentage': 42.86}

### It is not a jscpd behaviour change

`minTokens: 50` is the default in `@jscpd/core` **3.5.10**, **4.0.1**, and **5.x** (verified by
unpacking each published tarball). The default has never differed, so no jscpd major-version
change can explain this.

### It is not fixture drift or a detector regression

`tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py` and
`src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/_jscpd.py` were both introduced by a single commit,
`dabf4c6ce2` ("3ba0: add shared jscpd duplication analyzer", 2026-07-23), and **neither file
has been modified since** (`git log --follow` returns exactly one commit for each).
`--min-tokens` has never appeared anywhere in the source (`git log -S`).

**Therefore the test was born RED.** It has never passed against a real jscpd on any version.
CI skips it (jscpd is not installed there), so nothing ever observed the failure until a
developer with jscpd on PATH ran the suite.

### AC3 — duplication is NOT silently zero (runtime proof through the real adapter)

    rebar.metrics.analyzers.jscpd_dup.analyze(...) on jscpd 5.0.14:
      ticket fixture (32 dup tokens)  -> {'clones': 0,   'percentage': 0.0}
      same shape, >50 dup tokens      -> {'clones': 1,   'percentage': 48.81}
      real tree src/rebar             -> {'clones': 194, 'percentage': 1.748}

The adapter's report parsing is fully compatible with jscpd 5.x and reports real clones on
real trees. The zero is specific to a sub-threshold fixture.

### Disposition

Fix the fixture, not the assertion: enlarge the duplicated fragment comfortably past the
documented 50-token floor so the test exercises the detection it claims to guard. The
assertions `clones >= 1` / `percentage > 0` are unchanged. A negative control is added so a
future genuine detector failure cannot pass vacuously.

compiled_state.description:
## The defect

`tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py::test_live_clone` fails against a real,
installed jscpd. The adapter reports `duplication["clones"] == 0` for a fixture that contains
two byte-identical files, so the assertion `result.duplication["clones"] >= 1` fails.

    assert 0 >= 1

## Why this is being filed now

This failure was one of the two used as evidence in bug a5f5 (`make worktree` provisioned its
venv from ambient python3, so worktrees ran Python 3.14 while CI tested 3.11-3.13). a5f5's
acceptance criteria required re-checking both on an in-matrix interpreter, because every prior
observation of them had been on an untested Python and nobody could say which were artifacts.

Re-checked on Python 3.12.13 as part of landing a5f5:

- `tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py::test_full_backend_account_is_present`
  -> PASSES. It was an artifact of the untested interpreter, and needs no ticket.
- `tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py::test_live_clone`
  -> STILL FAILS. So it is genuinely unrelated to the Python revision.

## Environment

    jscpd     5.0.14  (/opt/homebrew/bin/jscpd)
    python    3.12.13 (in-matrix)

The test is a live-tool test: it is skipped when jscpd is absent, so CI (which does not install
the Node toolchain) never runs it. It only fires for developers who have jscpd on PATH for
`rebar metrics`, which is why it has gone unattributed.

## Likely direction, not yet confirmed

jscpd 5.x is a major version ahead of whatever the adapter was written against; the most likely
cause is a changed report shape or changed default thresholds (`--min-lines` / `--min-tokens`)
so the fixture's clone falls under the detection floor. Confirm before fixing — this ticket
records the observation, not a diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Root cause established: adapter contract vs jscpd 5.x behaviour, with evidence.
- [ ] `test_live_clone` passes against the installed jscpd, or the adapter's supported jscpd
      range is declared and the test skips outside it (loudly, naming the range) rather than
      failing.
- [ ] `rebar metrics` duplication is confirmed to report real clones on jscpd 5.x, not silently
      zero — a metric that reads 0 when it means "I cannot tell" is worse than `unavailable`.

## Provenance

Discovered from a5f5 while satisfying its "re-check on an in-matrix interpreter" criterion.
